report.tagline: Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal's AI company, which set out to build Indian AI models and chips and has pivoted to renting AI computing as a cloud.
report.simpleSummary: Krutrim was started in 2023 by Bhavish Aggarwal, who also runs Ola and Ola Electric. The plan was to build India's own AI: chatbots that speak Indian languages, AI models and even AI chips. It became India's first AI unicorn in 2024. By 2026 it had shut down its Kruti assistant app, dropped chip plans, cut staff in several rounds and turned into an AI cloud company that rents computing power to businesses.

overview.whatItDoes: Krutrim today mainly sells AI cloud services: businesses rent GPU computing and use hosted AI models through Krutrim's platform, with data kept in India. It earlier built its own models (Krutrim-1 and Krutrim-2) tuned for Indian languages and a consumer assistant called Kruti, which went offline in 2026. Its Bodhi AI chip plans have been dropped.
howItWorks: Developers and companies sign up on Krutrim Cloud and pay for GPU time or per-use access to AI models.
Krutrim hosts its own models and popular open models, such as Llama and DeepSeek, on servers in India.
Enterprise tools help companies build chatbots, voice agents and document tools in Indian languages.
Ola group companies like Ola and Ola Electric are early and large users.
Ola Electric pledged part of its shares to fund a data centre for Krutrim.
overview.valueProposition: AI computing and models hosted in India, priced in rupees, with Indian language support, for companies that want local data storage.

businessModel.summary: Krutrim now makes money by renting AI computing (GPUs) and hosted AI models to businesses, billed in rupees. A large share of early demand comes from Ola group companies. It gave up on making money from a consumer assistant and paused its chip plans.

revenueStreams.detail: Companies pay per hour or reserve GPUs for months.
Developers pay per token to use hosted models.
Custom bots and tools for companies, sold under contract.
Ola, Ola Electric and related firms buy computing and AI services; exact share not public.

businessModel.pricing: Pay-as-you-go GPU and model pricing in rupees on Krutrim Cloud; enterprise pricing not public.
costDrivers: Buying or leasing GPUs, mostly from NVIDIA
AI researchers and engineers (reduced after layoffs)
Sales and support for enterprise clients
businessModel.unitEconomics: For a GPU cloud, the money is in keeping GPUs busy. If Krutrim pays roughly ₹150 to ₹250 an hour to own and run a high-end GPU, and rents it for ₹250 to ₹400 an hour, it makes money only when the GPU is rented most of the day. Idle GPUs lose money fast. Model APIs add margin on top of computing. Selling to Ola group firms fills capacity but may not prove outside demand. All rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Ola group companies as first customers
Bhavish Aggarwal's public profile and 'build AI in India' message
Cheap hosting of popular open models, such as DeepSeek, to attract developers
Enterprise sales in mobility, fintech and e-commerce
Government push for AI computing in India (IndiaAI Mission)
whatBringsUsersBack: Workloads already running on Krutrim servers
Rupee billing and Indian data storage needed for compliance
growth.moat: Krutrim's moat is thin. Its main edge is Indian data centres, rupee billing and the Ola group as an anchor customer. Global clouds (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) also have Indian regions, and other Indian GPU clouds like Yotta and E2E Networks compete on price.

competitors.positioning: Indian AI startup building Indic models, backed by the IndiaAI Mission.

competitors.name: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
competitors.positioning: Global clouds with Indian data centres.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: They offer far more services; Krutrim competes on price and local focus.

improvementIdeas.problem: Layoffs make companies doubt Krutrim's reliability.

improvementIdeas.idea: Free credits for Indian AI startups in exchange for 12-month commitments
improvementIdeas.problem: Krutrim needs outside customers to fill GPUs.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher GPU utilisation and less reliance on Ola.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Paid GPU hours from non-Ola customers

improvementIdeas.idea: Indic voice agent kit for banks and telecoms, priced per call in rupees
improvementIdeas.problem: Companies need Hindi and regional language support bots but lack AI teams.

pmLessons: A big mission ('build India's AI') is not a product. Pick one problem you can win first.
Competing with free global assistants for consumers needs far better quality, not just local branding.
Pivoting to what customers pay for (computing) can save a company, but it changes what you are.
Revenue from your own group companies is a good start, but outside customers prove real demand.

interviewQuestions.question: Krutrim shut down its Kruti assistant. Why do you think it failed, and what would you have done?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at quality versus ChatGPT and Gemini, distribution, and the cost to serve free users. Suggest a narrower use case, like Ola-only tasks.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Krutrim and Sarvam's strategies for building Indian AI.
interviewQuestions.hint: Krutrim moved to cloud; Sarvam kept building models with government support. Compare revenue now versus long-term value and risk.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Krutrim's north star metric be now?
interviewQuestions.hint: Paid usage from outside customers. Break it into new customers, GPU utilisation, usage per customer and reliability.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you win enterprise customers after news of layoffs?
interviewQuestions.hint: Address risk directly: SLAs, data export options, references. Pick one segment, like Indian fintechs, and set a pilot metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Krutrim keep training its own models?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost, talent and differentiation against hosting open models. Suggest small Indic models only where they beat open ones.
